title.narrative: Strengthening Youth Capacity to Effectively Manage their Fiscal and Natural Resources in Kenema Dist

description.narrative:
This project seeks to empower youth in three mining chiefdoms in the Kenema district to influence transparent and accountable management of natural resource wealth so as to minimize conflict and enhance communal benefits.
Land lease agreements reached between government and mining companies,have mostly, not been community-friendly. One reason is because investing companies normally use the top-bottom approach to acquire land. In that process, they most often dictate the bargain to their advantage, while the actual land holding families play the underdog. Mining communities are mostly not involved in the process of determining whether exploitation of natural resources should or should not take place. Mining communities, which are supposed to be the richest communities are rather the poorest communities in the country and suffer most from environmental and social hazards caused by irresponsible mining activities. Issues of low education, discrimination, lack of livelihood options mostly affect the youth in mining communites and impede their development.
